newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Malan sees 7-10 pct inflation 1997 - papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Malan sees 7-10 pct inflation 1997 - papers.

text.p: Brazilian inflation should reach between seven and 10 percent in 1997, according to Finance Minister Pedro Malan, local newspapers said on Saturday.
Brazil last had single-digit inflation in 1951, 1952 and 1957, Malan added.

"The Brazilian economy is clearly recuperating....GDP growth in the third quarter of 1996, compared with that of 1995, was up seven percent and up 3.6 percent compared with the second quarter of this year," he was quoted as saying.
"With these figures it is possible to predict a GDP growth of between four and 4.5 percent next year," said Malan.
This would be an increase on an estimated 3.1 percent growth in 1996.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
